title: Settings Active Link Class
prompt: A React settings nav link needs active styling. Write a helper that returns "link active" when href exactly matches currentPath and "link" otherwise.

explanation.beginner:
Example: settingsActiveLinkClass("/home", "/home") produces "link active". Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Compare “leaves other links inactive”: input ["/settings","/home"] produces "link". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Tempting mistake: Selecting a display position after a list changes can identify the wrong item. Use the domain key when matching two collections.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “leaves other links inactive”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
